items.title: Innovation & Management in Tourism
items.description: The bachelor's programme in Innovation & Management in Tourism imparts comprehensive knowledge in hotel and destination management, leisure businesses, tourism organisations and e-tourism companies. Special emphasis is also placed on the further development of social skills.

items.title: International Business Relations
items.description: The bachelor's programme in International Business Relations imparts specialised knowledge in the following areas: business administration, law, controlling, logistics export, marketing, tourism management, wine management, language and communication, international economics as well as economic policy, business law and economics. Lecturers include renowned international experts; languages are taught by native speakers. Students have the possibility to acquire additional qualifications such as project management and Cambridge business certificates within the framework of the curriculum. Potential employers will be companies operating on a national and international level and organisations with business relations with the EU or Central and Eastern Europe.

items.title: Tourism and Leisure Management (E)
items.description: In an age of rapidly changing global markets prospective managers constantly face new challenges. The bachelor's degree in Tourism and Leisure Management provides you with the tools that are necessary to succeed in this environment locally and internationally. The aim of this English-language bachelor's programme is to acquire with in-depth business administration expertise. The tourism and leisure industry is the centre of attention throughout the programme.

items.title: Business Administration with a Focus on Tourism & Hospitality Management
items.description: The bachelor's degree programme in business administration with a focus on tourism & hospitality management is unique because it combines the special features of tourism and hospitality management studies with a bachelor's degree programme in business administration. This means that the basics of business administration such as accounting, marketing and human resources management are taught specifically in the context of tourism and hospitality management.

items.title: Tourism & Hospitality Management
items.description: Tourism moves people and people move tourism. As experts, graduates shape the tourism of the future - sustainably and with innovative approaches. Competent, practice-oriented and international, this means a business education with a focus on tourism and a solid basis for a career in service management.

items.title: Award in the risks & medical aspects of diving
items.description:
This study unit offers information to the students on certain important health and safety issues relating to diving/freediving. It should be used along with the information of the industry code of practice, and used in the development of risk management procedures at a workplace.
a)	Comprehensively demonstrate how to evaluate if a dive center is organized in a way medical aspects are taken into consideration and the dive center or pro is aware of diving medical and fitness guidelines, under the guidance of a Diving Safety Officer (DSO)- II. a)	Comprehensively identify the risks & medical aspects of recreational and technical diving.
b)	Systematically understand the need and reasons behind a medical fit to dive certificate. The learner will be able to:
a)	Comprehensively identify what are the medical & health aspects of diving.
b)	Comprehensively identify which are the medical and fitness aspects of diving.
c)	Systematically understand the Health & safety aspects for recreational diving.
d)	Systematically understand malaria (travel diseases) and diving.
e)	Systematically understand Decompression illness.
f)	Systematically understand what is emergency management and treatment.
g)	Systematically understand ear and sinus problems.
h)	Systematically understand medication and diving.

items.title: Bachelor of Science (Honours) Food Science (Food and Wine)
items.description:
This course intends to provide a solid background for individuals interested in pursuing food related careers.  It offers a comprehensive scientific preparation for employment or entrepreneurial activities in the food service industry or related professions, including tourism operators, agri-food producers and specialists in the gastronomic field.  

To complete this specialisation students must follow these three compulsory modules (i. Wine Cellar Management; ii. Food Wine Pairing iii. Food and Wine Marketing).
1.	Discuss different cuisines, healthy diets and eating habits, food safety and hygiene, and the benefits of specific kinds of food.
2.	Deliver presentations on food issues and create web applications for marketing purposes.  
3.	Nurture links with the specialised press and publish articles in magazines on the food and wine culture.
4.	Organise promotional events and marketing campaigns, and conduct consumer surveys and professional interviews.
5.	Create relationships between culture and food to enhance the territorial identity and promote traditional and artisanal foods - cheeses, breads, sweets, wines and other typical products.
6.	Manage communications with customers through the different social media.
7.	Engage with specialists in the food and wine industries, using the proper technical terminology and interpreting correctly the text of current agri-food legislation.
8.	Raise customers' appreciation of certified quality products, highlighting their distinctive features and preparation techniques.
9.	Inform the public on how to ensure the authenticity of agri-food products and detect food fraud.
10.	Exploit the menu as the restaurant's marketing tool, and ensure specific dishes get the right visibility.
11.	Promote more sustainable food products, such as local and organic ones, produced in a more environmentally friendly way.
12.	Enhance the aesthetic presentation of agri-food products and dishes, and organise tasting sessions to underscore their sensory appeal. 1.	Broaden experience on the professional roles and work environments in the catering and hospitality industries, in order to make the right choices on career, future learning and self-development options.
2.	Enhance critical and creative thinking skills, as a tool for problem solving.
3.	Work in a team to deliver the desired outputs within the given deadline.
4.	Apply quality management and control systems, as well as ethical responsibilities throughout one's professional career.
5.	Create innovative food products and deliver practical projects in a work environment.
6.	Develop independent learning and skills complementary to the catering industry (e.g., knowledge of a foreign language, proficiency in the use of computers, application of professional software and online tools).

items.description:
The advent of social networks (Web 2.0), Internet of Things (Web 3.0) and other technologies (e.g. Blockchain) has opened up new opportunities for operators in the leisure-related tourism sector such as the sports and diving sector, that were previously unavailable.  It has also presented new challenges that need to be addressed in order for the operators in this sector to take advantage of all the opportunities being made available.
Distinguish the characteristics of typical Web 2.0 applications such as social networking sites, wikis, blogs, podcasts, RSS, Google.  (Specific examples related to the fields of hospitality and heritage will be illustrated).
b) Define the ‘Web 2.0 tourist’, which in many ways represents a different group of persons when comparing their characteristics to the more classical tourist.
c) Acquire and understand the fundamental principles required to develop a Web 2.0 strategy applicable to the tourism, particularly the diving tourism sector. The learner will be able to:
a) Learn to use the various Web2.0, Web3.0 tools in order to extract information relevant to the diving sector
b) Evaluate the potential use of diverse tools when applied to specific scenarios (recreational diving, marketing, technical diving, risk assessment, hazard identification and prevention etc.)
c) Develop and apply a strategy incorporating these technologies and evaluate its effectiveness within the (diving) business envrionment. Have a clear understanding of what constitutes the web 2.0. That is the ‘second generation’ of web-based services.
b) Appreciate the fundamental characteristic of Web 2.0 – the notion of people being able to collaborate and share information in previously unavailable ways.  There is also the possibility for users to generate new information on the web which needs to be analysed by (tourism) organisations and use it to market specific products and services to specific groups if not individual users.
c) Be aware of the ways that the Web 2.0 tourist uses some of these tools in order to obtain information (prices, reviews, travel tips,..) and how these may influence the actual choice of a destination and associated services.

items.description:

items.title: Bachelor of Arts (Honours) Tourism Studies
items.description:
The main objectives of the Tourism Studies programme are to provide a comprehensive background to the local and international dimensions of the tourism industry and to equip students with skills to critically analyse the tourism industry and its impacts on society,  the environment and the economy. It is an inter-disciplinary programme,  covering a wide range of subjects.    Students will also be expected to carry out two supervised industry placements,  where they will gain valuable work-place insights and skills. In Year II,  students are encouraged to apply for student exchange programmes for one or two semesters at one of the universities which have links with the Institute for Tourism,  Travel and Culture.    The Institute for Tourism,  Travel and Culture works closely with local tourism stakeholders,  such as government entities and ministries,  hotels,  restaurants,  heritage agencies,  and is an active member of several European and international networks. These links ensure that programmes of study offered by the Institute are relevant and useful for anyone who wishes to develop an interest or career in the tourism sector.

items.description:
The College’s Bachelor of Arts/Bachelor of Business Administration Business and Management suite of programme awards are designed for students who are looking to develop their careers towards managerial and executive positions in business organisations, public sector organisations and voluntary sector organisations. • To produce graduates who, through workshop sessions, syndicate discussions, exercises, role plays and sensitivity training, are able to demonstrate advanced managerial communication skills; • To produce graduates who are able to demonstrate advanced understanding of key themes in business and management scholarship (and, as appropriate, relevant sub-disciplines), with a critical understanding of relevant underpinning policies and principles; • To produce graduates who are able to work highly effectively in teams, demonstrating advanced and excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to function sensitively and productively when working with others; and, • To produce graduates who are appreciative of the benefits of lifelong learning skills such as time-management, group working, effective communication, planning and leadership in whatever field of business and management (and, as appropriate, relevant sub-disciplines) they may operate within.

items.title: Award in Sustainability in Tourism and Hospitality
items.description:
This module aims at examining the theoretical and applied dimensions of the concept of sustainable tourism and hospitality and how these evolve in time. A number of factors,  notably: the economy; planning; the environment and social aspects will be addressed in relation to the promotion of sustainable tourism and hospitality development. Furthermore,  this module will discuss core aspects of pedagogy and the appropriate techniques and methods that should be employed to teach this subject effectively to students using the relevant syllabus provided by the local education authority.
Identify the core principles of sustainable tourism,  the cultural construction of the key concepts,  key drivers and implements these principles; Use models of Limits of Acceptable Change related to the Hospitality and Tourism sectors.  Apply the knowledge obtained in this course to teach students the necessary material according to the relevant syllabus. The Concepts of Sustainable Development; Interpretations of Sustainable Development; Critical Analysis of Sustainability and how it is related to the Global Tourism and Hospitality Sectors; Cotemporary Debates of Sustainable Tourism; Environemntal,  Economic and Socio-Cultural aspects of Sustainable Tourism; The Environment - Land Use Management/Social and cultural Issues/CSR; The concept of Limits of Acceptable Change in relation to the impact of the Tourism and Hospitality sectors. Methods and techniques of teaching sustainable tourism to studetns using the relevant syllabus provided by local eucation authority. Properly understand the implications of global and local environmental issues and their causes; Utilise a scientific approach in case studies and on tourism and hospitality related concerns; Initiate concepts of sustainable development and the principles of sustainability in the workplace; Foster various economic,  environmental and social aspects which are of special relevance to tourism; Conduct basic environmental audits and simple visitor flows; Utilise specific tools regarding planning and management strategies with a specific focus on the local scenario; Carry out self-directed and lecturer-directed research; Manage various research initiatives related to sustainable tourism and present findings to peers in a suitable manner. Teach Sustainable Tourism to students using the relevant pedagogical techniques and methods to deliver information

The programme is delivered on a full time basis mode in each key area with the help of student centered learning approach. The whole programme is highly interactive and it is expected to enrich the students’ knowledge in key tourism management areas; sharpen their managerial skills; and enhance their professional competence in today’s highly dynamic travel and tourism environment.
The learner will be able to; Improve his / her understanding of the main aspects of key tourism management skills by working effectively through people; Practice speaking skills in the controlled environment of workshop sessions through syndicate discussions,  exercises,  role plays and sensitivity training; Work highly effectively in teams,  demonstrating excellent interpersonal skills and excellent ability to function sensitively and productively when working with others Enhancing the knowledge and strengthening the practice of tourism management written skills through class room assignments,  case study workshops,  examinations and market report analyses; Demonstrate a confident understanding of themes in tourism management scholarship,  with the ability to identify and conceptualise the critical factors involved,  critically review existing evidence in order to support an interpretation;  Demonstrate a confident and complex understanding of travel and tourism challenges with the help of the application of the learner’s acquired knowledge and skills; Explore and test a range of viable solutions,  propose innovative strategies based on research and knowledge;  Research,  evaluate,  interpret,  discuss and source a wide range of scholarly material in tourism management areas; Demonstrate excellent awareness of globalisation and the importance of cultural insight in travel and tourism management.

items.description:
The main objectives of the Tourism Studies programme are to provide a comprehensive background to the local and international dimensions of the tourism industry and to equip students with skills to critically analyse the tourism industry and its impacts on society,  the environment and the economy. It is an inter-disciplinary programme,  covering a wide range of subjects.    Students will also be expected to carry out two supervised industry placements,  where they will gain valuable work-place insights and skills. In Year II,  students are encouraged to apply for student exchange programmes for one or two semesters at one of the universities which have links with the Institute for Tourism,  Travel and Culture.    The Institute for Tourism,  Travel and Culture works closely with local tourism stakeholders,  such as government entities and ministries,  hotels,  restaurants,  heritage agencies,  and is an active member of several European and international networks. These links ensure that programmes of study offered by the Institute are relevant and useful for anyone who wishes to develop an interest or career in the tourism sector.

items.title: Award in Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA)
items.description:
This study unit introduces students to Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) Initiative: the promotion of a culture of safety at dive businesses. A program that focus the attention of all parties invested in this industry to reduce unnecessary, avoidable and repeated accidents.
The learner will be able to:
a)	Comprehensively identify the Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) approach:
•	Staff health and safety.
•	Staff Training and certification.
•	Training pool.
•	Training room.
•	Dive shop.
•	Dive operations.
•	Dive boat.
•	Cylinder filling area.
•	Air quality.
•	Equipment storage.
•	Instrument workshop.
•	Vehicle safety.
•	Travel safety. a)	Comprehensively demonstrate how to perform a risk assessment in a dive business. a)	Perform a risk assessment in a typical dive operation.
b)	Demonstrate how to write a HIRA report, under the guidance of a Diving Safety Officer (DSO) - II.
